extract.text: On the other hand, possibly because he divined in Buck a dangerous rival, Spitz never lost an opportunity of showing his teeth. He even went out of his way to bully Buck, striving constantly to start the fight which could end only in the death of one or the other. (3.2)
extract.context_before: As Buck grows accustomed to the brutal life of a sled dog, he becomes locked in a rivalry with Spitz, the lead dog, for dominance of the team.

questions.question_text: In what ways are Buck and Spitz similar? How are they different from each other?
key_points: Similarities: Both dogs were strong/ fit/ alpha males
Highly competitive/ proud
Differences: Buck is imaginative/loyal/ a survivor – quick thinking/ Fights savagely but only when provoked
Spitz is devious/ treacherous/ cruel and pugilistic (meaning he'll readily start a fight)

questions.question_text: Why is Buck regarded as the protagonist (the hero) of Jack London's book 'The Call of the Wild'?
key_points: The evolution of Buck's character is the focus of the story.
The novel traces his life from the time he is a happy four-year-old basking in the California sun to a tough competitor
Buck emerges as a faithful, loyal companion, and finally to the leader of a wolf pack in the wild.
Buck is noble, admirable, and shows remarkable loyalty (to Francois and Perrault) and love (for Thornton) - protagonist-like qualities.

questions.question_text: Explore the themes of love and loyalty as revealed in the relationship between Buck and Thornton in Jack London's novel, 'The Call of the Wild'.
key_points: Buck's love and loyalty to Thornton is the result of extremities of circumstance – they save each other's lives on more than one occasion.
Thornton saves Buck's life on different occasions (from death by club/starvation/will to die)
Buck in turn saves Thornton's life when he gets in a bar fight.
On another occasion Thornton almost drowns but is again saved by Buck.
Thornton wins a huge sum of money by betting Buck can pull an enormous load.
Thornton goes in search of gold and a lost cabin with his partners and is killed by natives.
Buck seems unable to respond to the call of the wild until after Thornton's death.
This suggests that perhaps his love and loyalty for the man are stronger than his more primeval urges.
